rows.note: Desert cacti rest cold and almost dry; watering then only makes weak growth (Clemson, RHS).
Low nitrogen, half to a quarter of the label dose. Excess N makes soft tissue that rots (Clemson, Iowa State).
One size up only, and wait several days before the first watering (Clemson).
Minimum 6-8 h. Moving a plant outdoors needs half shade first, or the leaves scorch (Iowa State).
Water at 17-22 C, never softened water, and empty the saucer (Clemson).
Indoor plants are fed only through the growing season, nothing during the resting months (UConn).
Philodendron and relatives root from stem cuttings at any time of year (Clemson).
Never let it dry out completely, and never leave standing water in the pot (Clemson).
Nothing at all for 6 months after dividing or repotting; too much fertiliser burns the fronds (Clemson, UConn).
Split the root mass into 2-3 sections and keep soil and air humid for weeks afterwards (UConn).
Dry indoor air in the cold months is the real risk; a pebble tray beats misting (Clemson, UConn).
Deep and even. Shallow, patchy watering cuts calcium transport and causes blossom-end rot (USU, UGA).
Stone fruit takes three split doses and none in the last weeks of summer, so growth hardens off (Clemson).
Dormancy is the standard window: structure is visible and the wound closes in the next growing season (USDA).
The natural drop at 1-2 cm does not replace hand thinning; keep the largest fruit of each cluster (Iowa State).
Roses drop to half dose in the peak heat and stop 6 weeks before the first expected frost (Clemson).
Seed heads left standing feed wildlife through the cold months (Clemson).
Feed at emergence OR after flowering, never both. Remove the spent flower but never the leaves (Illinois).
1-1.5 gallons per inch of trunk diameter, over the root zone and not against the trunk (Penn State).
A mature tree needs little or none. Late feeding with high nitrogen delays dormancy (Clemson).
Spring-flowering shrubs are pruned right after the flowers; prune later and you cut off next year's buds (Clemson).
Keep it 3-5 in clear of a young trunk and 8-10 in clear of a mature one (Penn State).
Soak until it runs out of the holes, then drain. Never leave it standing in the saucer (AOS, RHS).
Half the label dose, little or no urea, and skip every 4th feed to flush salts (AOS, RHS).
Only once new root growth is visible. In sphagnum, repot after it finishes flowering (Clemson).
Holiday cacti only: 14+ h of unbroken dark for at least 6 weeks, and 2 h of lamp light cancels the buds (Clemson).
Split group: Mediterranean herbs want real drying, leafy ones (basil, parsley, mint) want steady moisture (Clemson, RHS).
Rosemary in the ground gets none at all, and very rich soil dulls the flavour (RHS, Clemson).
Rosemary takes a light trim after the flowers, never into old wood. Mint is cut to 5 cm to renew it (RHS).
Early morning, just before flowering, is when the leaf carries the most oil (Clemson).
Rosemary survives -8 C once established, but frost still burns the new shoots (RHS).
